analysis.title: Nuclear Nuggets: Global reactor tracker - October edition; 3Q26 Preview
key_insights: Nuclear equities underperformed over the past three months: GS nuclear coverage averaged -21% versus +3% for the S&P 500 (data as of 10/9/2026), a 24% gap. Weakness was spread across SMR and uranium-exposed names.

OKLO fell 29%, the weakest in GS coverage, which GS attributes to risk-off sentiment toward advanced nuclear developers and limited near-term commercial catalysts. SMR fell 21% as investors focus on timing of definitive commercial agreements and project awards. UEC fell 13%.
Short interest over the past month: SMR +16% (largest increase), OKLO +1%, UEC -14%, which GS reads as some covering and relatively more constructive positioning in uranium-focused names.

Hyperscaler power demand deals continue: Google-Constellation agreed to add 890 MW across 11 existing reactors through uprates (10/6), Constellation-Amazon signed an agreement supporting ~$3B of investment at Calvert Cliffs including 190 MW of added capacity in 2030-2032 (10/1), and Google signed with Georgia Power to support fleet uprates (9/22).

US DOE offered Vistra a loan to support reactor upgrades and uprates adding ~102 MW (10/6). The NRC completed its environmental review of the Crane Clean Energy Center (former Three Mile Island Unit 1) restart (9/28).
The US and South Korea are targeting deployment of six AP1000 and two APR1400 reactors in the US under a new nuclear cooperation framework (10/1).

SMR licensing milestones: the NRC issued the first US construction permit for a BWRX-300 at Clinch River, Tennessee (9/30). Holtec's SMR-300 got approval for early site work at Palisades (9/16) and submitted its Preliminary Safety Analysis Report (10/2). Blue Energy filed its first NRC construction permit application (9/16).
Bechtel will step away as EPC contractor for TerraPower's Natrium project in Wyoming after the current phase. TerraPower says the project remains on track with a successor EPC strategy.
Samsung C&T invested ~$110M in Kairos Power (9/22). The EIB agreed to invest up to EUR 40M in Finland's Steady Energy, its first SMR investment (9/15).

Europe policy: Dutch Senate removed the 2033 shutdown date for Borssele (possible life extension to 2054) and the Dutch government agreed to buy 70% of operator EPZ for EUR 115.7M plus EUR 119M of capital support. Italy's Senate approved a framework for advanced reactors and SMRs. UK regulators outlined plans to speed approvals. Poland advanced AP1000 EPC negotiations with the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium.

China: Tianwan Unit 7 connected to the grid for the first time (10/8), Changjiang Unit 3 entered commercial operation (9/17), and Bailong Unit 2 first concrete was poured (9/28). Japan's Chubu Electric withdrew Hamaoka 3 and 4 restart applications to pursue decommissioning.
Reactor tracker: 38 reactors under construction globally as of 10/10/2026, with China adding one. 2026 has seen 5 grid connections and 10 construction starts, with no permanent shutdowns.

Spot U3O8 held around $89.50-$90/lb through September and early October. September spot volume was the lowest monthly level since December 2009. Long-term U3O8 price was unchanged at $96/lb with limited change in offer levels despite active utility term-market engagement.
Sprott Physical Uranium Trust did not buy in September and retains ~2.1mn lbs of potential purchases for the rest of the year.

Fuel cycle: Cameco signed an offtake with Global Laser Enrichment, Centrus and Antares signed a multi-year HALEU supply deal, Framatome signed its first commercial higher-enriched fuel contract with TVA, and General Matter filed an NRC licence application for a Paducah enrichment facility. Bannerman Energy completed an AUD124M raise and expects a Final Investment Decision on Etango in Q4 2026.

GS rates Standard Nuclear (STDN) Buy with a $18 price target, and Oklo (OKLO) and NuScale (SMR) Neutral. OKLO target cut to $49 from $57 and SMR target unchanged at $6 (the SMR EV/Sales multiple cut to 1X from 1.5x).

market_movers.rationale: 12-month target is a 50/50 weighting of DCF (~$19/sh) and EV/EBITDA ($18/sh) valuations. Key 3Q26 call topics are contract backlog conversion, Antares option volumes and capacity expansion beyond 2.5 MTU.
Target cut to $49 from $57 on a lower terminal multiple (17X from 20X on lower comps) in the DCF and a 2033 EBITDA basis. 2026E-2028E adj. EBITDA now ($235mn)/($200mn)/($174mn).
Target unchanged at $6, but the EV/Sales multiple was cut to 1X from 1.5x due to lack of operational updates. Call focus is TVA PPA timing and ENTRA1 pipeline expansion.

sector_views.rationale: Coverage averaged -21% over three months versus +3% for the S&P 500. GS cites risk-off sentiment toward advanced nuclear developers and limited near-term commercial catalysts. Two of three rated names are Neutral.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 preview for STDN (Buy), OKLO (Neutral) and SMR (Neutral): GS lists topics to listen for rather than giving EPS or revenue estimates.

OKLO estimate changes: 2026E-2028E adj. EBITDA revised to ($235mn)/($200mn)/($174mn) from ($235mn)/($197mn)/($186mn), due to changes to opex and D&A and modest revisions to reactor deployments. These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.
STDN call topics: contract backlog conversion, Antares option volumes, SN-TN and SN-ID authorization and ramp timing, capacity expansion beyond 2.5 MTU, Project Janus deployments.

OKLO call topics: Aurora-INL execution and 2028 startup visibility, plutonium allocation, commercial traction and customer funding, Ohio campus interconnection, isotope commercialization, deployment scalability following Groves criticality.
SMR call topics: TVA PPA timing, ENTRA1 pipeline beyond TVA, first project timing, supply chain readiness, hyperscaler and industrial customer traction, RoPower path toward FID.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Unchanged. Utilities are active in the term market but offer levels have barely moved.
-3% over one month and -6% over three months.
Flat over one month, +8% over three months and +13% over twelve months.

risk_factors: STDN: dependency on the success of early-stage customers, uncertain timing of regulatory licensing approvals, competition and feedstock availability.
OKLO: liquidity needs to reach sustainable FCF, securing fuel for the deployment ramp, competition, and timing of the combined operating and construction license.
SMR: execution risk, customer risk, cash burn and financing needs, end cost of modules on delivery, competition and licensing.
Goldman Sachs is manager or co-manager of a pending underwriting for Oklo, a conflict of interest disclosed in the report.
